records.current_summary:
For a trans visitor the operative risk in Ceará is sustained lethal exposure: the jurisdiction recorded 11 killings of trans and travesti people in 2024 — the region's highest toll and third nationally — and 8 in 2025, tied for the highest state total of that year's 80 nationwide; two consecutive years at the top of the ranking indicate an entrenched environment rather than a statistical blip. There is no state-level legal distinction: the national constitution and penal code apply uniformly.

The national victim profile sharpens the exposure for a visibly trans traveller: 97% of victims are travestis and trans women, over half aged 18–29, 70% of those with recorded race are Black, 97% killed in public spaces with most incidents outside capitals.

prison_adds.title: LGBTQ people in prison
prison_adds.summary: Wikipedia overview article (fetched and read in full, 28 Sep 2026). Its international-standards sections show trans-prisoner placement norms elsewhere (Scotland's 2022 inspection standards admitting trans and intersex prisoners to facilities matching lived/experienced gender; Canada placing by gender identity), but its Brazil paragraph contains no placement rule - only that traumatic social vulnerability and stigma for travestis and transgender people shape rehabilitation. Negative evidence: this general overview reports no codified Brazil-specific trans-prisoner housing policy.

prison_adds.title: LGBT rights in Brazil
prison_adds.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBT rights in Brazil' (fetched and read in full, 28 Sep 2026) states, in its Politics section, that LGBTQ people have a special place in Brazilian prisons, separate from other prisoners; that transgender people ('transsexuals') have the right to be called by their social name and not their birth name and to be forwarded to women's prisons; and that LGBTQ prisoners may choose male or female clothing. The statement is footnoted (ref. 253) to a Mix Brasil (UOL) article, 'Vivemos uma inercia no congresso...', archived 18 Jan 2012 - i.e. c.2012-era support for placement-follows-identity in Brazil; treat as dated evidence, recency not re-verified.

records.current_summary:
The risk signal for this jurisdiction is a violence-rate spike: zero recorded trans killings in 2024 jumped to 4 in 2025 — the sharpest deterioration in the dataset. Against a population of ~3.5 million, four cases yield approximately 1.14 killings per million per year, the highest per-capita rate among all 27 units in 2025 and roughly three times the national figure of ~0.38/million. The dataset cautions against reading a single-year zero as safety and notes the volatility.

For a visitor, the small absolute numbers mean a single incident dramatically shifts perception, and the volatility suggests the environment can turn rapidly. No state-level statutory restriction or unique legal finding applies; the risk is purely a violence-rate signal.

For a trans visitor the risk in Pernambuco is violence-exposure concentrated in the interior: the jurisdiction recorded 7 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, behind only the two 8-count units in the dossier's ranking of that year's 80 national killings. Roughly two-thirds of such killings happen in interior cities rather than state capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policy are weaker — so a visibly trans visitor in mid-sized and interior municipalities is in the geography where the recorded danger actually concentrates, alongside a victim profile of young (majority 18–29), overwhelmingly Black (70% of those recorded) travestis and trans women.

No jurisdiction-specific legal restriction or ordinance was identified in the audited sources; the national framework applies uniformly.

records.current_summary: Highest legal floor in the country: the first sanctuary-state law for transgender care (SB 107, signed 2022) and shield protections against out-of-state enforcement. But also the most recorded incidents of any state in 2025 (198, GLAAD ALERT), a "dramatic increase" in Los Angeles hate-crime reports, and 34 recorded killings of trans women 2008–2025 (4.1 per 100k). Above the national score 0.36; law and street volume pull opposite ways.

prison_adds.title: LGBTQ rights in the United States (Wikipedia) — Housing of transgender inmates by state
prison_adds.summary: Wikipedia article (fetched, HTTP 200) stating that as of January 2021 California is the one state that allows transgender people to be housed in prison according to their gender identity, while New Mexico is the one state with separate facilities reserved for transgender people only; the article's U.S. state map legend codes California under 'Allows transgender inmates to be housed according to their gender identity' and notes the same context that federal policy returned to assigned-sex-at-birth placement after January 2017 guidance was rescinded. Placement axis: identity-based housing within the general population, with no trans-only separate facility documented for California.

prison_adds.title: LGBTQ rights in California (Wikipedia) — Prison policy
prison_adds.summary: Wikipedia article (fetched, HTTP 200) whose prison policy coverage documents that in 2015 California became the first state to fund gender-affirming surgeries for transgender prison inmates, and cites KPBS reporting (2015) on 'Transgender In Prison: How California's New Guidelines Will Be Implemented' — CDCR's operational guidelines governing transgender inmates. Thin on the housing axis: the article confirms the identity-based care and guidance posture but contains no explicit statement of a trans-only unit or segregation practice.
